independence: Each role was filled by separate fresh claude-opus-5-5 sessions (subject x3, safety x2, language x2, lessons split by count), each given only its own role's work orders (openlessons jury orders) and told never to open another role's orders or verdicts; verdicts were written to per-role folders and combined only by jury run after all seven sessions had finished. The drafting model (claude-fable-5) sat on no role.

notes: subject: keying the Moon as 'what we see in the night sky' teaches the common misconception that the Moon belongs to the night: it is often seen in the daytime and is not seen on some nights (new moon). Ask instead about the stars (NGSS: stars other than the Sun are visible at night but not during the day), or say 'often' and accept moon and stars.

claims.claim: The sun appears to rise in one part of the sky, move across it, and set; patterns of the sun, moon and stars can be observed and predicted.
